Subcortical mapping during resection identified the arcuate fasciculus at a distance of 8 mm from the tumor cavity, causing phonemic paraphasias. The tumor was highly vascular and fibrous; a gross total resection of the enhancing nodule was achieved while leaving a small 3 mm rind over language-positive cortex. During resection, the patient suffered a focal seizure manifesting as speech arrest and right facial twitching, aborted with cold saline irrigation and a 2 mg bolus of midazolam. Speech returned to baseline within 5 minutes. Hemostasis was secured with bipolar and Surgicel. The dura was closed primarily and the bone flap replaced.
